card.title: Drop the Armor
card.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've locked the shop. You can stop doing the cheerful voice for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone has to keep morale up. You're my only employee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm off the clock. What did that empty till do to you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the stockroom. Then I practised smiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You don't owe me a second performance. Can we lock the stockroom and let you be upset out here?

mechanism: A asks a shop owner to stop maintaining morale and allow distress to be visible in a trusted relationship.
confusable: Unlike requesting an explanation alone, A must persuade B to drop the performance of strength.
comparison: D108-a invites grief out of the stockroom; D108-b rejects a promise of cheerfulness as the price of company.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
